about.title: About RGB to HEX Converter
description: This RGB to HEX converter helps translate color values into the format that a stylesheet, design handoff, or component token expects.

It is useful when a color comes from an editor, screenshot, design tool, or code sample in one format and needs to be reused consistently in another. The point is not only to convert the syntax, but to reduce copy mistakes in design and front-end workflows.

howTo.title: How to Use the RGB to HEX Converter

steps.title: Enter the RGB values
steps.description: Start with the red, green, and blue channel values if your source color is coming from a graphics tool or script.

steps.title: Check the color preview
steps.description: Use the preview to confirm you are converting the intended color rather than a nearby value caused by typing or paste mistakes.

steps.title: Copy the HEX output
steps.description: Use the HEX result when you need a compact code for CSS, design tokens, or a color variable list.

steps.title: Verify the target context
steps.description: Make sure the place you are pasting into expects a plain HEX value, a leading hash, or another color format entirely.

tips: RGB channels must stay in the 0 to 255 range.
HEX is often easier to paste into CSS, but RGB can be easier to reason about during debugging.
If a color looks almost right but not exact, recheck one channel value before assuming the converter is wrong.

faq.q: When is HEX more useful than RGB?
faq.a: HEX is often more convenient in CSS, token files, and quick handoff notes because it is compact and widely recognized in front-end workflows.

faq.q: When is RGB more useful than HEX?
faq.a: RGB is easier to inspect when you need to think in individual channel values, compare intensity changes, or work in tools that expose red, green, and blue sliders directly.

faq.q: What is the most common color conversion mistake?
faq.a: Copying the wrong channel value or forgetting the leading hash in a HEX code. Both mistakes can produce a result that looks valid but is not the intended color.

faq.q: Does converting RGB to HEX change the color?
faq.a: No. The format changes, but the underlying color should stay the same if the original RGB values are correct.

faq.q: Why should I still check the preview if the math is simple?
faq.a: Because workflow errors usually happen before or after the conversion, such as copying the wrong number, pasting into the wrong field, or mixing up two similar colors.

faq.q: Can I use this for design handoff?
faq.a: Yes. It is useful for handing colors from mockups to code, especially when one side of the workflow prefers RGB and the other prefers HEX.
